subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB525 LANDED - THE 'GREATER THAN ZERO' HALF IS NOW ENFORCEABLE, BECAUSE ZERO IS NO LONGER THE ABSENT-PHRASE SENTINEL. The footing AREA was always right ([footing start, page size] INCLUSIVE - pinned at the boundary by Gr26ab_CounterEqualsBody_IsFootingEopNotOverflow and its goldens). What was not implemented was GR3's 'The value shall be greater than zero and not greater than integer-1 or the value of the data item referenced by data-name-1', because ONE integer slot carried two different facts: 'the footing start' and 'there is no FOOTING phrase', with 0 encoding the second. The fix is the SHAPE, not the guard: LinagePage.Footing is int?, SequentialIoEmitter.LinageOpExpr renders null for an OMITTED phrase (TOP and BOTTOM stay int - GR1 says their values ARE zero when absent, so only FOOTING had a collision), EvaluateLinage applies GR6 b) 2 to every footing start that IS specified including 0, and the GR26 b) end-of-page arm's guard became `_footing is { } f` - a test of PRESENCE rather than of value. THE DISCRIMINATING PAIR is on disk: Gr6b2_FootingPhraseHoldingZero_IsAViolation_NotAnAbsentPhrase and Gr1_NoFootingPhrase_SamePageAndWrite_IsAnOrdinarySuccessfulWrite are the same page size, the same WRITE, differing only in whether the FOOTING phrase is written - a model that encodes absence as 0 cannot tell them apart, which is exactly what used to happen (the first one printed NO-EOP / LC=005 like the second). A specified footing of 0 is now the §13.18.34.4 GR6 b) 2 violation, reported as I-O status '90' with the EC-I-O-LINAGE condition - see GR-13.18.34.4-6.
